explanation: A full parabola fails the horizontal line test, so it has no inverse - two x's share each y. By restricting the domain to x >= h (right of the green line) we keep only the rising half, which is one-to-one and CAN be inverted. The inverse is the mirror image across the dashed line y = x: every point (x, y) on f reflects to (y, x) on f-inverse. Drag h to slide both the restriction and its mirrored inverse together.
bullets: Restricting to x >= h makes f one-to-one, so an inverse function exists.
f and its inverse are reflections of each other across the line y = x.
Swapping a point's coordinates (x, y) -> (y, x) lands you on the inverse.
